app.title: Simple-Todo
app.description: A simple local-first peer-to-peer TODO list app using OrbitDB, IPFS and libp2p

todo.empty: No TODOs yet. Add one above!

replication.pending: Waiting for this OrbitDB entry to be replicated by the relay.
replication.pinned: The relay confirmed that this exact OrbitDB entry was replicated and stored locally.
replication.unavailable: No exact relay replication proof is currently available for this entry.
replication.unknown: Relay replication status was not observed for this existing entry.

toast.dropped: ⚠️ {peer} closed the connection shortly after connect

networkConfig.label: Network config
networkConfig.description: Validates the configured browser-reachable relay addresses and prepares the libp2p transports and services.

libp2p.label: libp2p
libp2p.description: Creates and starts the libp2p node, including its peer identity, discovery, relay, WebSocket and WebRTC support.

helia.label: Helia
helia.description: Starts the Helia IPFS node on top of libp2p and enables block exchange and HTTP retrieval.

orbitdb.label: OrbitDB
orbitdb.description: Loads or creates the persistent OrbitDB identity and initializes OrbitDB using the Helia node.

database.label: Database + sync
database.description: Opens the shared todo database, loads its local operation log and starts OrbitDB pubsub synchronization.

localTodos.label: Local todos
localTodos.description: Connects the local todo store and starts hydrating it from OrbitDB in the background without blocking the application.

webrtc.label: WebRTC connected
webrtc.description: A live libp2p connection using WebRTC is available. This normally appears after another browser peer has been discovered.

relay.base: A live WebSocket connection to a relay/bootstrap peer is available for discovery, pubsub and circuit relay traffic.
relay.noHealthUrl: No HTTPS health URL can be derived from the connected relay address.
relay.loading: Reading the OrbitDB relay version from {origin}/health…
relay.verifiedVersion: OrbitDB relay version {version}; health and peer ID verified at {origin}/health.
relay.verifiedNoVersion: Health and peer ID verified at {origin}/health. This relay does not expose its OrbitDB relay version.
relay.unverified: {origin}/health could not be verified, so its OrbitDB relay version is unavailable.

consent.warningBody: This is a working demonstration rather than a finished product. It does what it says, and the format may still change - so keep anything you would be sorry to lose somewhere else as well.
consent.accept: I have read this and accept it
consent.remember: Don't show this again on this device
consent.storageMemoryHint: Todos are stored in a shared, unencrypted OrbitDB database in memory and will be deleted on app reload or on exit.
consent.storagePersistentHint: I understand todos are stored in a shared, unencrypted OrbitDB database in the browser's IndexedDB and will persist between app restarts or after app exit.
consent.relayLabel: Connect to the public libp2p relay network
consent.relayHint: On: peers find each other automatically through public relay and bootstrap nodes. Off: this browser connects only to peers you invite yourself with a QR code or a copied invite — nothing announces you, and nobody can find you.

clause.noServer: We run no server, and no copy of your list exists anywhere we control.
clause.gateway: The app itself is delivered through a public IPFS gateway, which sees that you loaded it. Your own Kubo node, or the IPFS Companion extension, fetches it from the network instead.
clause.relayOn: Relay and bootstrap nodes introduce peers to each other, and may cache or replicate this demo data so another device can collect it later.
clause.relayOff: No relay is contacted. Without one, the other device has to be reachable from this network.
clause.persistent: Your todos are kept in this browser and survive a restart, in a shared and unencrypted database.
clause.memory: Your todos live in memory only and are gone when this page reloads. The database is shared and unencrypted either way.
clause.cookies: No tracking cookies are used. If you tick "don't show this again", that choice is the only thing saved on this device.
